writeup.headline: F5 rates Hold: excellent quality and net cash, offset by a valuation expensive against its own history.
writeup.thesis: F5 scores 62, a Hold, just 3 points short of the Buy band. The strongest supports are the balance sheet (score 100, net cash and no debt) and quality (score 84), with a gross margin of 81.9%, operating margin of 24.5%, FCF margin of 29.3% and diluted share count down 1.6% year on year. Growth is middling (score 54), with TTM revenue growth of 9.4% and latest-quarter revenue growth of 10.8% year on year, and growth slowed by 0.2 pp from the previous quarter. Valuation is the main drag (score 41): in absolute terms P/S of 6.3x, P/FCF of 21.3x and EV/EBIT of 23.5x are not low, with FCF yield 0.3 pp below the 10-year Treasury yield, and the stock is expensive against its own history, for example P/S is more expensive than at 53 of the last 61 month-ends. Trend is neutral (score 53): the price is 14.9% below its 50-day average and 23.8% below its 52-week high, though shares are up 50.9% from 12 months ago to 1 month ago.
key_risks: FY27 guidance of 8% to 9% revenue growth points to slightly slower growth than the recent TTM revenue growth of 9.4%.
Management flagged memory-cost pressure on gross margin, and the Q1 EPS guide midpoint came in below consensus.
Analysts warn the hardware refresh cycle is waning; Piper Sandler downgraded to Neutral.
Valuation is expensive against its own history, leaving room for multiples to compress if growth disappoints.
Pending securities class action and derivative suit over the 2025 breach, plus two distributors made up about a third of FY25 revenue.
what_would_change: A 3-point gain in the composite score would move the rating to Buy, for example from improved valuation as the price falls or earnings grow, or a recovery in the price trend.
Faster revenue growth or stronger AI-related bookings lifting the growth score would also push toward Buy.
A drop to Sell would need an 18-point fall, such as a sharp margin decline from memory costs combined with weaker growth and negative news.
